title: add-benchmark-lab-mixed-workload-reporting-pipeline-v46
author: Ethan Zhang
ci_status: pass (initial failure on docker build fixed, re-ran)
description:
Motivation: expand the Benchmark Lab to cover mixed realistic production-like workloads and provide a consolidated reporting pipeline (v46) that produces pct/latency buckets, per-model KV-cache hit metrics, and multi-variant profiling baselines. This PR adds representative mixed-workload runners (conversational + embeddings + reranking), updates profiling baseline artifacts, and wires a new reporting pipeline that aggregates results into the metrics service and S3 for downstream analysis.

What changed (high-level): added a new mixed_runner harness that composes conversational and embedding workloads with configurable ratios; added workload spec files for representative mixes; added profiling baselines and a script to generate baseline artifacts; implemented reporting_pipeline_v46.yaml that defines parallel collectors, aggregation jobs, and a final uploader; added CI test job to validate mixed-runner end-to-end in the benchmark lab docker image; small ergonomics and docs updates.

Why: previous profiling suites covered isolated workloads (chat-only or embeddings-only). Product teams asked for a single benchmark that better approximates production shapes to improve model selection and quantization recommendations (ENG-1982). The new reporting pipeline standardizes aggregation and reduces engineer time spent gluing results together.

Compatibility and rollout: default reporting pipeline is opt-in via a new config flag in benchmark-lab/config.yaml. Existing nightly jobs are unchanged until teams flip the opt-in flag. The baseline artifacts are additive; no existing artifacts are removed.

Testing and validation: unit tests for runner orchestration and parsers added; integration test in CI builds a benchmark-lab docker image and runs a small mixed workload (100 requests) to validate end-to-end dataflow; reporting pipeline validated against local minio in integration job; perf-run verification produced stable latency distributions on internal infra (NVIDIA A10g) with KV-cache hit metrics present in the final payload.

Migration notes: teams that want to adopt the mixed runner should add a new schedule in the benchmark-lab pipeline and point to mixed_workloads.yml. The reporting pipeline requires credentials for the metrics uploader; see docs/benchmark-lab/reporting/README.md for setup steps.

Follow-ups: (1) add traffic-weighted model selection logic to the runners (ENG-2104), (2) extend runner to support bursty arrival patterns in the next iteration, (3) add a Grafana dashboard for v46 aggregated metrics.
